label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
**November 11, 2026**

**To:** Mrs. Okafor
**Copy:** Darlene [last name], Transportation Office, for my personnel file
**From:** [Your name], Driver, Bus 41, Route 9
**Re:** Written statement in response to the complaint dated October 29, 2026, about the afternoon of Tuesday, October 27

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

My supervisor gave me your complaint on November 3 and asked me to answer it in writing. This statement goes in my file with the Transportation Office and a copy comes to you, so I am writing it to you directly. I would rather you hear my side from me.

Before the details, I understand why you were scared. I have grandchildren. If I were waiting on one of them and watched the bus pull away with her still on it, I would be upset too, and I would want an answer. So here is what happened from the driver's seat.

On Tuesday, October 27, I was driving the afternoon run on Bus 41, Route 9, out of Fairmont Elementary. Amara's stop is Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. The schedule has me there at 3:50, and I pulled up at 3:52. Amara has the green tag on her bag, which tells the driver an adult has to be at the stop before she gets off. I looked for an adult at the corner and did not see anyone. I waited until about 3:55 and still did not see anyone at the stop.

The district rule for kindergarten riders is that if no adult is at the stop, the student stays on the bus and goes back to school, and the office calls the parent. That is not left up to the driver. At 3:56 I radioed dispatch and told them I had a kindergartner with no adult at the stop and would be bringing her back. Gloria at dispatch called Fairmont to let them know. I had three more stops to make and 14 students still on board, so I finished the route and drove back to the school. We got to Fairmont at 4:31. I walked Amara into the office myself and left her with Mrs. Petrakis.

Your complaint says you were parked across Brandt by the laundromat and that you waved at me. I am not saying you were not there or that you did not wave. I am telling you I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street that afternoon. If I had seen you, I would have waited for you to come over and let Amara off like any other day. I had no reason to do anything else.

I also could not get out and look. With 14 children on the bus, I cannot step off and walk across a road to check parked cars. I would not leave your daughter alone on a bus to go looking for somebody else's parent, and I could not leave those children to go looking for you. All I have to go on is what I can see from the seat and in my mirrors.

The complaint says I "took" your daughter. I kept her on the bus and brought her back to her own school, into the office, and I did not leave until she was with a staff member. That is what the rule calls for.

The complaint also says I drove off laughing. I was not laughing. As we pulled out, a fourth grader in seat 2 had stood up, and I was telling that student to sit back down. From across the street that may have looked like something else. Nothing about that stop was funny to me.

Amara was fine the whole ride. I told her we were going on a little extra trip. She colored on her folder and asked me if she could ride more. She was not crying or frightened at any point.

I have been driving a school bus for 28 years and have never had a write-up. In all that time I have had to take a kindergartner back to school one other time, with a different family, years ago. That family thanked me afterward. I mention it only so you know this is not something I do often or without thinking.

I am sorry you had a bad afternoon and that you spent any part of it not knowing where Amara was. I am not going to apologize for following the rule, because the rule is there for her. If I let a kindergartner off at a corner because I figured somebody was probably close by, and I was wrong, that would be far worse than what happened on the 27th. I would make the same call again.

Bus 41 has a camera on board. I am asking the Transportation Office to pull the footage from the October 27 afternoon run at Kessler and Brandt, from the time I pulled up to the time I pulled out. It will show how long I waited, what could be seen at the stop, and what I was doing as we left. I would like it reviewed and the result noted in my file with this statement. I have no objection to the office telling you what it shows.

Going forward, I have one request. Please wait on the bus side of the street at the corner. If you need to wait in your car, please step out when the bus pulls up so I can see you. As long as I can see you, Amara gets off.

I am glad to keep driving Amara and I want this settled between us. I will be at her stop tomorrow the same as always.

Respectfully,

[Your name]
Driver, Bus 41, Route 9

---

Fill in your name and Darlene's last name, and change the date at the top if you turn it in on a different day. The last line says "tomorrow," so change that too if it would land on a non-school day.
